newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end slightly up, banking shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end slightly up, banking shares fall.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday on a technical rebound, while liquid institutional investors cautiously began accumulating shares, brokers said.
But bankings shares declined as investors remained disappointed with financial reform proposals by the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform, they said.
The composite stock index rose 4.36 points to 723.35, off the day's low of 716.51.
With many investors on the sidelines, trading volume fell as 39.81 million shares changed hands against last week's average of 60 million.
"The proposals fell far short of investors' anticipation as they wanted big conglomerates to be allowed in bank management," Lee said.

Brokers said investors were not excited with the reform proposals scheduled to be presented to President Kim Young-sam on Friday. Proposals include the expansion of the bank ownership limit to 10 percent under certain requirements.

Shipbuilders and carmakers rebounded even though the yen was still in a consolidation against the dollar in world markets. Daewoo Heavy rose 340 won to 7,390 and Ssangyong Motor added 90 won to 5,250.

The Securities Supervisory Board said it had found illegal trading in shares of Taeyang Metal Industrial Co, New Start Trading and Ilyang Pharmaceutical. The securities watchdog had reported persons allegedly linked to the unfair trading to prosecutors.

Taeyang Metal opened at its lower-limit of 38,200 and then rebounded to close at 44,200. New Star remained unchanged at 58,000, off its low of 54,000 and Ilyang ended at 24,200, recouping from its low of 23,500.
Brokers forecast the market would gradually rise unless the yen fell sharply. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
